query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: Provides a qualitative categorical axis for crew demeanour (friendly/professional/indifferent/rude/neutral) that goes beyond the numeric 'Staff Service' rating, giving a genuine grouping variable for isolating advantage attributes of high-rated airlines. Values in the samples are well read from the text (welcoming/kind→friendly_attentive; well-trained on hospitality→professional_efficient). In the seat-complaint sample where crew is unmentioned it filled 'neutral_adequate' rather than 'unknown', which is a mild unsupported assertion but a defensible default.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_legroom
per_column.rationale: Useful as a qualitative seat/legroom axis that adds cabin-condition and pitch nuance beyond the numeric 'Seat Comfort' score, and it correctly returns 'Unknown' for the silent row (sample 3). However groundedness is undermined by the 'spacious_comfortable_flatbed' label being applied to clearly economy contexts: a 1h45 economy flight (sample 1) and an economy 3-3-3 older aircraft (sample 4) that describe only spacious legroom / comfort, not a flatbed. Conflating 'spacious economy legroom' with 'flatbed' invents a specific the text contradicts.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: A distinct-in-principle facet (speed/helpfulness of service), but across all five samples it moves in lockstep with cabin_crew_attentiveness (friendly/professional→proactive_helpful), so much of its signal is a near-restatement of that column, reducing its independent analytical leverage. Values are mostly sound readings of the text, though for the seat-only complaint (sample 2) it asserts 'adequate_available' where service is unmentioned — a mild unsupported fill rather than 'unknown'.

judge.rationale: All three columns convert free-text reviews into categorical service/comfort attributes that are directly relevant to identifying advantage attributes of high-rated airlines, giving analysts new axes to group and compare against Overall Rating. They add qualitative granularity beyond the existing numeric Staff Service / Seat Comfort scores. Weaknesses: customer_service_responsiveness overlaps heavily with cabin_crew_attentiveness in the evidence (partial redundancy), and seat_comfort_legroom shows a recurring grounding fault where 'flatbed' is asserted on economy flights the text describes as merely spacious/comfortable, contradicting the source. Silent-row handling is inconsistent (correct 'Unknown' in one case, but unsupported 'adequate' fills elsewhere).
